source.title: Training Beyond Convergence: Grokking nnU-Net for Glioma Segmentation in Sub-Saharan MRI
source.authors: Mohtady Barakat; Omar Salah; A. Yasser; Mostafa Ahmed; Zahirul Arief; Waleed Khan; Dong Zhang; Aondona M. Iorumbur; Confidence Raymond; Mohannad Barakat; Noha Magdy

record.file_problem: The main paper text is present, but the text cuts off during reference 15.
record.tranche_reason: The study extends grokking-like prolonged training to glioma MRI segmentation, a non-algorithmic image task. It does not reproduce the original algorithmic-data setup.
record.gate_note: The study compares validation metrics from 200- and 3,500-epoch nnU-Netv2 runs. Figure 3 is described as showing training by 100 epochs, overfitting at 1,000 epochs, and grokking after 1,000 epochs, but the text does not provide training/test accuracy values or a numerical time course. The hybrid results in Tables 3–4 combine the two models and do not isolate the extended run's effect, so they are not recorded as separate rows.
record.test_reason: The study frames a 3,500-epoch nnU-Netv2 run on BraTS-Africa MRI as grokking, but its results cannot show a grokking-like delay. It compares only final validation metrics from a 200-epoch and a 3,500-epoch run. The 200-epoch baseline already generalizes well (Dice 0.866 ET, 0.863 TC, 0.923 WT), not near chance. No validation or test time course is given; Figure 3's claimed 'overfitting in 1000 epochs, grokking after' has no numbers. The extended run also re-initializes the learning-rate schedule with a 1e-4 floor, which confounds training duration. It varies no initialization scale or weight norm. The findings measure 'extended training gives modest gains', a related but different construct, so they go under fits_no_version rather than as a test of V3.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is mostly correct. The abstract claims they 'were able to achieve grokking'. The conclusion is more modest: extended training improved ET and TC while WT stayed largely unchanged. They recommend a hybrid using the 3,500-epoch model for ET/TC and the 200-epoch model for WT.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies prolonged training to nnU-Netv2 for 3D MRI segmentation, not the original small algorithmic-task setup. It compares 200 with 3,500 epochs; the extended run also re-initializes the learning-rate schedule and sets a minimum learning rate of 1 × 10⁻4.
record.method_sensitivity: Training duration and tumor region affect the reported outcome: extended training improves ET and TC metrics but does not improve WT metrics. The extended run also uses a different learning-rate schedule from the baseline.

fits_no_version.finding: Extending nnU-Netv2 training from 200 to 3,500 epochs gives modest gains on 3D glioma MRI segmentation. ET Dice rises 0.866→0.902 and TC Dice 0.863→0.901, while WT is unchanged or slightly lower across metrics. The extended run re-initializes the LR schedule with a 1e-4 floor.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prolonged training beyond convergence (with an LR restart) yields small late validation gains on some subregions in small-data medical segmentation. This is continued improvement, not a demonstrated grokking-like delay.

record.problems: The comparison reports final validation metrics rather than a numerical training/test accuracy trajectory, so it does not establish the claimed chance-level test period or precisely when generalization rises. There is no significance test; uncertainty is reported only as standard deviations for lesion-wise metrics. The training set has 55 cases and validation metrics use 35 cases. The baseline and extended runs also differ in learning-rate scheduling.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. Figure 3's loss progression is not recorded as a grokking/generalization outcome because the text gives no numerical values for it. Hybrid results in Tables 3–4 combine the two runs and do not isolate the extended run's effect.

untested.parts: No algorithmic data, no train/test accuracy trajectory, no training-set-size dependence.
No validation time course showing delay after training saturation. Baseline is not near chance. No initialization-scale or weight-norm manipulation, no lazy-to-rich test.
Weight decay fixed at default 3e-5. No critical dataset size or ungrokking test.

missing.what: Training/validation loss curve said to show training by 100 epochs, overfitting at 1,000, and grokking after 1,000. No numbers are given, and it is the only time-course evidence for a delay.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V3 'supports' and 'limits_scope' labels are dropped. Endpoint Dice gains of about 0.04 from a high baseline, with a confounded LR restart and no validation trajectory, cannot establish grokking-like delayed generalization or its control by the training regime. Lesion-wise gains lie well within the reported SDs (about 0.2), and there is no significance test. N=35 validation cases; single seed per run.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses MRI segmentation data, not small algorithmic datasets, and does not report training and test accuracy trajectories or dependence on training-set size.
No generalizing circuit, Fourier algorithm, memorizing component, or continuous circuit-progress measure is analyzed.
The study tests extended training on medical images, but does not vary initialization scale or weight norm, or test a lazy-to-rich transition.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning is studied.
Weight decay is left at the nnU-Net default; the study does not test its role, compare circuit efficiency, or examine a critical dataset size or ungrokking.
The study does not identify or compare algorithms learned across runs.
The study does not test adaptive-optimizer or softmax numerical-instability explanations, or control these as potential artifacts.

relation.reason: The stated objective and experiments investigate whether prolonged training produces grokking in MRI segmentation; Figure 3 explicitly presents training dynamics as evidence. This tests the non-algorithmic-delay component of V3, although the available endpoint metrics do not establish it and initialization or norm switching is untested.

tranche.reason: The study investigates grokking in a new, non-algorithmic segmentation setting using its own experiments. Section 2.6 and Figure 3 describe a training/overfitting/grokking time course, so the rationale that it reports only endpoints overlooks relevant evidence. The endpoint rows cannot establish delayed generalization, but an inconclusive test does not make this T6.

source_check.notes: Figure 3's caption identifies training at 100 epochs, overfitting at 1,000 and grokking afterward; its curves are not reproduced in the extracted text. The abstract swaps baseline ET/TC scores; Tables 1–2 and §3.2 agree with the recorded rows.

reader_labels.condition: Enhancing Tumor and Tumor Core validation metrics after 3,500 epochs
reader_labels.reason: The extended run has higher Dice scores for both regions than the 200-epoch run (R01–R02); the reported surface and lesion-wise metrics also increase for these regions (R04–R05, R07–R08, R10–R11, R13–R14, R16–R17).

reader_labels.condition: Whole Tumor validation metrics after 3,500 epochs
reader_labels.reason: Whole-tumor Dice is essentially unchanged and the reported whole-tumor lesion-wise and surface metrics are lower in the extended run (R03, R06, R09, R12, R15, R18).
